transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Harbor CTO), Elena Morales (Harbor Platform Eng), Jamal Thompson (Harbor ML Ops)
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Usage and cost trends reviewed; Harbor seeing spike in daytime inference and a heavy tail of long sequences from clinical note stitching.
- Discussed right-sizing Dedicated vs Hosted, burst capacity, and VPC options for sensitive PHI workloads.
- Agreed to run an end-to-end benchmark and to exchange token-level traces; Redwood to provide tailored pricing projection and quantization recommendations.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, can you hear me ok?
[00:02] Daniel Park: yes, loud and clear, thx. we got a small agenda, mostly health and cost readout, and then roadmap alignment.
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: hi all, marco from embed infra, i'll cover the latency/cost suitation and suggested knobs we think will move the needle. couple of assumptions up front, correct me if i'm wrong: you're running 3 models in prod, majority is the clinical-summarizer at 2.7k avg tokens per request is that right?
[00:22] Elena Morales: that's close, the average is around 1.8k but there's a heavy tail to 6k when notes get concatenated, our daytime peak qps is about 45, tails hit 80 during month-end reporting.
[00:34] Jamal Thompson: and important to note, for PHI workloads we need VPC + KMS and audit logs retained 365d. SOC2 is a checkbox for legal.
[00:44] Avery Chen: got it, thanks. quick recap of what we measured since last check-in — usage up ~28% month over month, token spend up 39% due to longer sequences, and your median latency is within the SLO but p95 slips around the midday spike.
[01:00] Daniel Park: the p95 is our blocker, product teams keep complaining. they put agressive latency targets because clinicians need short turnarounds, but we also can't blow the budget.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. a few levers: 1) split your long-document flow into chunked pre-processing so average seq len drops, 2) use KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, 3) consider a quantized variant for background jobs, 4) Dedicated capacity with reserved pools to reduce jitter.
[01:28] Elena Morales: tell me more about kv cache — we tried something but it was brittle and it interfered with our context merging.
[01:36] Marco Ruiz: yeah, implementation matters. Redwood's KV cache is per-conversation prefix caching; for your summarizer we can cache the static preface and reuse keys across similar records. we also can tune cache TTL and shard placement to avoid cold cache storms. note the runtime will fallback to the hosted model if cached variant misses and there's a route-policy you can set.
[01:56] Jamal Thompson: fallback worries me if it sends PHI to hosted endpoint — our legal requires data never egress a VPC unless it's encrypted under our KMS and auditable. how does that work?
[02:08] Avery Chen: good question — for Private/VPC we keep inference within your network. Dedicated also supports customer-managed KMS for model keys; we can set route policies that restrict model variants to private pool only. if a private pool is saturated we can configure soft-fallback or hard-reject, your choice.
[02:22] Daniel Park: whoa hard-reject seems scary for uptime. can we have canary fallback to a de-identified flow?
[02:29] Priya Nair: we actually prototyped a de-identification preprocessor you could run in your VPC — it strips PHI before calling hosted models. we'll share the doc link after the call.
[02:38] Elena Morales: please do. also, what's typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated? numbers we can show exec?
[02:46] Marco Ruiz: rough ballpark — for steady throughput Dedicated can be 35-55% cheaper per token when amortized on reserved pools and correct batching; but initial commit and pool sizing needs care. Hosted is easier to start and cheaper at very low volume but scales out cost-wise under sustained high qps.
[03:01] Daniel Park: helps. one of our engineers said Redwood Dedicate had better tail latency — is that accurate?
[03:07] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated reduces multi-tenant jitter because pools are isolated and you can tune GPU scheduling to your seq-len distribution. we also offer predictable KV cache locality and prefer kernel selection logic for your model. but only if we size it correctly.
[03:20] Jamal Thompson: sizing is our pain point. we ran out of burst credits last month and auto-scale didn't keep up. what's changed?
[03:26] Avery Chen: we noticed your autoscale policy was very conservative with cooldowns. recommendation: increase burst buffer (we can provision on demand) and tighten the autoscale metric windows so scaling happens earlier. Marco will propose a concrete autoscale policy.
[03:38] Marco Ruiz: i'll share a template — it includes a 15m short-window spike policy and a longer smoothing window. also suggest enabling predictive-burst which pre-warms a small set of nodes based on historical day-of-week patterns.
[03:51] Elena Morales: predictive warm sounds good, but are there cost implications?
[03:54] Marco Ruiz: small extra charge when pre-warmed nodes are idle, but it avoids costly cold-start heavy tail. we'll show the math in the projection sheet.
[04:05] Daniel Park: about quantization — could we get the same output quality after 4-bit quant? clinicians care about hallucinations, so we can't degrade onsite accuracy.
[04:15] Marco Ruiz: quantization can introduce minor quality drift depending on the model family. our Optimize team runs evals on your prompt set. for background batch jobs, 4-bit often works well; for high-sensitivity clinical responses we recommend hybrid: FP16 or int8 on critical routes. we'll run an automated eval against your prompt samples during the bench.
[04:32] Priya Nair: i'll coordinate the evals with Jamal. Jamal can you share a representative prompt set (redacted) so Marco's team can run quality regressions?
[04:40] Jamal Thompson: yes, we have a 150-prompt eval set. we'll scrub PHI and share it by Thursday.
[04:45] Daniel Park: timeline — product wants to pilot Dedicated for a 3-month pilot starting Feb 1st. what do we need to get there?
[04:53] Avery Chen: ideal runbook: 1) exchange token traces and seq histograms (customer), 2) Redwood proposes pool size + pricing and bench windows (redwood), 3) run 2-hour bench on production-like infra and report, 4) sign commitment and provision Dedicated pool. we can compress those into two weeks if Harbor prioritizes the traces and grants infra access.
[05:12] Elena Morales: access is the blocker — our infra team needs a scoped service account. do you have a checklist for the bench?
[05:19] Marco Ruiz: yes, checklist includes S3 artifact location, anonymized payloads, expected peak QPS, latency SLOs, allowed fallbacks, KMS config. i'll paste the checklist link in the follow-up.
[05:28] Jamal Thompson: we also need SSO integration for RBAC. can Redwood integrate with our Okta SCIM?
[05:33] Avery Chen: yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning; we also support fine-grained RBAC per-route. we'll open a ticket with Security to run a scoping workshop.
[05:43] Daniel Park: one more thing— audit log retention 365d is non-negotiable. do you ship logs to our SIEM?
[05:50] Marco Ruiz: yes, we can stream audit logs to your splunk/elastic endpoint or push to an S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS key. retention policy can be set on your side.
[05:59] Elena Morales: ok good. curious about model rollouts — we need canary A/B for 10% of traffic and auto-fallback if quality drops. how mature is Redwood's rollout tooling?
[06:09] Marco Ruiz: rollouts are first-class. you can specify canary ratios, roll forward/rollback rules, and quality gates tied to eval sets. for your use case we'd recommend 5% canary with a 30 minute observation window, automated rollback on p95 or quality regressions.
[06:25] Jamal Thompson: if we detect a regression do we get a dump of the failing prompts? that's essential for debugging.
[06:30] Marco Ruiz: yes, we can capture redacted prompt + response pairs and surface them in the console with tags. we can also emit traces to your tracing system.
[06:40] Daniel Park: cost transparency is a selling point for our CFO. can you provide token-level billing and per-route dashboards so we can attribute spend to teams?
[06:48] Priya Nair: that's already in the Console — per-route token breakdown, per-token cost, and cost-per-conversation. we can grant read-only access to your finance leads.
[06:55] Elena Morales: great. any special notes about data residency? we need EU residency for EU patient data.
[06:59] Avery Chen: we have region pins and can host data and inference within eu-west-1 or other compliant regions. for Private deployment we can package near-shore. we'll include region options in the pricing sheet.
[07:09] Daniel Park: ok let's talk numbers — can you share a sample projection with current usage and a 3-month pilot?
[07:14] Marco Ruiz: yes i'll produce a 3-scenario projection: conservative, expected, and aggressive. the projection will show tokens, projected spend, and per-token unit economics under Hosted vs Dedicated with quantization options.
[07:24] Jamal Thompson: include the break-even point for commit amounts.
[07:27] Marco Ruiz: will do.
[07:30] [08:00] brief pause while people check notes and links shared in chat
[08:15] Elena Morales: small oddity — we've seen occasional transcriptions say 'KV cash' which confused the product folks. are you sure it's 'KV cache'?
[08:22] Marco Ruiz: yes it's KV cache, common transcription glitch.
[08:26] Daniel Park: before we close, can we summarize actionables and owners?
[08:30] Avery Chen: sure — 1) Harbor: export token traces + seq hist (Elena) by 2027-01-20; 2) Redwood: send detailed pricing projection & right-sizing (Avery/Marco) by 2027-01-21; 3) Redwood SE: schedule 2-hour bench window and share checklist (Marco) target week of 2027-01-25; 4) Harbor: share redacted 150-prompt eval set (Jamal) by 2027-01-21; 5) Priya to schedule follow-up exec QBR on 2027-02-08.
[09:00] Daniel Park: good, that's everything i think. thanks for the practical plan.
[09:05] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the projection.
[09:10] Elena Morales: thanks, bye.
[09:12] Jamal Thompson: bye.
